title: Advanced Blood Relations
tagline: Year 2 — Multi-step family chains, in-law relations and coded relations

introduction.overview: Advanced blood relation problems chain three or more statements, add in-law relations (through marriage), and use coded symbols such as A + B or A × B to describe relations. The method is the same as in Year 1: draw a family tree with generation levels and gender marks, and read the answer from the tree. The difficulty comes from length and from the ambiguity of neutral words, so careful reading and a neat diagram are essential.
introduction.placementRelevance: Blood relation questions with three or more links and coded relations are commonly asked in company reasoning rounds.
introduction.realWorldContext: Kinship terms in forms, insurance nominee records and genealogy charts all follow these relations.

learningObjectives: Build a family tree from three or more statements
Handle statements with "only" and with neutral terms
Choose a neutral answer when gender is not fixed

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Maternal = mother's side; paternal = father's side. Uncle/aunt are parents' siblings (and their spouses). Cousin: child of uncle or aunt. Brother-in-law/sister-in-law: spouse's sibling or sibling's spouse.

coreDefinitions: In-law relation: relation formed through marriage (father-in-law, mother-in-law, brother-in-law, son-in-law).
Great-uncle / great-aunt: sibling of a grandparent.
Coded relation: a symbol stands for a relation, e.g. + = mother of, − = brother of, × = father of.
Generation level: parents above, siblings and cousins at the same level, children below.
Neutral term: a word such as cousin, sibling, spouse, child, parent that does not fix gender.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Treat the relations as a path on a tree: go up to a parent, across to a sibling or spouse, down to a child. The answer is a name for the whole path. The challenge is to keep the gender and side (maternal or paternal) straight at every step.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Draw squares for males, circles for females, a double line for marriage, and vertical lines for parent-child. Place the person asked about at the end of a path from the starting person.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Path naming
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Up a parent, across a sibling, down a child = uncle/aunt's child (cousin)
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: Mother → her brother → his son = cousin

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: In-law rules
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Spouse's parent = parent-in-law; spouse's sibling = sibling-in-law; child's spouse = son/daughter-in-law

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Coded relations
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Read left to right: each symbol links two adjacent letters
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Write the chain, then name it.
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: A × B + C: A is father of B, B is mother of C → maternal grandfather

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Resolving "only"
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Unique person: "my mother's only daughter" = I (if female) or my sister
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: "Husband of my mother's only daughter-in-law" = my brother

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Neutral answers
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: If gender is not fixed, answer with a neutral term

mainNarrative: Start by marking genders from the statements (brother → male, sister → female, mother → female). Then place people on generation levels. In "A is the brother of B, B is the father of C", A is male at B's level, so A is C's paternal uncle.

For in-law relations, remember that marriage links two families. The wife's brother is the husband's brother-in-law. A husband's father is the wife's father-in-law. A son's wife is the daughter-in-law.

For coded relations, write the chain from left to right. A × B + C means A is the father of B and B is the mother of C, so A is the maternal grandfather of C. A − B × C means A is the brother of B and B is the father of C, so A is the paternal uncle of C.

Statements with "only" identify a single person. "Pointing to a man, Anita says: He is the husband of my mother's only daughter-in-law." Anita's mother's daughter-in-law is Anita's brother's wife, so her husband is Anita's brother.
When the gender of the answer is not determined, use a neutral term. The son or daughter of one's uncle is a cousin, and the person answers to "cousin" whichever gender.

deepDiveAspects.title: Great-relations
deepDiveAspects.content: The sibling of one's grandparent is a great-uncle or great-aunt. If D is sister of A, A is the father of B and B the mother of C, then D is the great-aunt of C.

deepDiveAspects.title: When two readings are possible
deepDiveAspects.content: Some statements fit two trees. In an exam, the options usually contain only one that works in both; if none does, the answer is "cannot be determined".

problemVariations.typeName: Chains of three or more statements
problemVariations.exampleSnippet: A is B's sister; B is C's father
Husband of my mother's only daughter-in-law

solvedExamples.title: Coded relation
solvedExamples.question: If A × B means A is the father of B, A + B means A is the mother of B and A − B means A is the brother of B, what does A × B + C mean for A and C?
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Read the chain left to right.

steps.title: A × B
steps.explanation: A is the father of B.

steps.title: B + C
steps.explanation: B is the mother of C.

steps.title: A and C
steps.explanation: A is the father of C's mother.

solvedExamples.finalAnswer: A is the maternal grandfather of C
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The father of one's mother is the maternal grandfather.

solvedExamples.title: Pointing statement with "only"
solvedExamples.question: Pointing to a man, Anita says, "He is the husband of my mother's only daughter-in-law." How is the man related to Anita?

steps.title: Mother's son's wife
steps.explanation: The daughter-in-law of Anita's mother is the wife of Anita's brother.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The wife of the brother is the daughter-in-law of the mother.

solvedExamples.title: A longer chain
solvedExamples.question: A is the brother of B. B is the father of C. C is the sister of D. D is the son of E. How is A related to E?

steps.title: B's children
steps.explanation: C and D (siblings) are children of B.

steps.title: E
steps.explanation: D is the son of E, so E is a parent of D and C; with B, E is the other parent.

steps.title: A
steps.explanation: A is the brother of B, who is E's spouse.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: A is the brother of E's husband.

shortcutMethods.title: Chain naming

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Try to hold the whole tree in memory.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Draw after each statement. For coded relations, write the chain and name it as a path: parent of parent = grandparent; sibling of parent = uncle/aunt.

rulesForApplication: Read the question from the right person.
Use neutral words if gender is open.

commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Label each link M or P.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Answering how C is related to A.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate options whose gender or generation clearly disagrees with the tree.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Draw a fresh tree for each question.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Coded relation questions are solved fastest by writing the chain.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I decode a three-symbol chain?
Can I solve a statement with "only"?
